Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Junction Health: MAP mosaic + proposed acceptance tests

Hi Elena —

Great talking yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a lightweight mutual action plan (attached) that separates milestone lanes (technical validation, security/compliance evidence, procurement & contracting, and pilot success metrics). The attached spreadsheet is intentionally concise — one row per major checkpoint with an owner, target date, and the acceptance test we'll use to validate the checkpoint.

A few high-level notes before you dive in:
- Pilot scope: 2 teams (Triage + Care Coordination), 10k messages/month traffic profile; target latency SLOs for interactive flows <= 450ms P95.
- Exit gates: we recommend a three-tier stoplight (green/yellow/red) for each KPI; green = proceed to next milestone, yellow = remediation sprint + re-test, red = pause and executive review.
- Acceptance tests: short, automatable smoke tests + 10 representative prompts per flow (we've sketched expected outputs and concordance thresholds in the PDF).
- Security queue: we flagged two SOC2 evidence items that typically slow procurement; if Junction can share the point of contact for InfoSec we can pre-stage the artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
1) You and Sam review the MAP draft and highlight any timeline or owner mismatches (reply by Wed 24th).
2) We run the pilot readiness checklist internally (Marissa will lead) and share a smoke-run on the 28th if timelines hold.
3) If procurement needs DocuSign changes, we'll queue them into the MAP under the contracting lane (Priyom to own).

Attachments: JunctionHealth_MAP_mosaic_v0.1.xlsx; acceptance-test-matrix_v0.3.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to syncing.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://www.redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Morris <elena@junctionhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@junctionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Junction Health: MAP mosaic + proposed acceptance tests

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful. Quick notes from our side after a first pass:

1) Timeline: our internal security review window opens 1 Apr, so the suggested pilot smoke-run on 28 Mar is probably optimistic unless you can share pre-staged evidence this week. Can Marissa and Priyom confirm what we can expect to see immediately?
2) Acceptance thresholds: the PDF lists a concordance threshold of 85% for triage intents. That feels low for our clinical triage use case — can you provide a short verification plan for precision/recall across the 10 prompts? We'll need to validate against our annotated set.
3) Contracting: procurement is OK with standard T&Cs but will require a data processing addendum (DPA) with specific retention windows. Sam will loop our legal team if we get to signature.

Cc'ing Sam so procurement and clinical product see these points. If we can get the security artifacts and the annotated sample results this week we can keep the MAP timeline intact.

Elena
Director, Clinical Platforms
Junction Health

Aisha / Priyom —

Quick internal note on the artifacts we can surface immediately:
- SOC2 scoping doc & recent attestation summary (redacted) — we can share a trimmed PDF by EOD Tue.
- Network topology diagram + VPC peering checklist — ready to share; I'll add to the Drive link.
- Annotated sample results: we can run the 10 canonical prompts against the pilot model and provide a per-prompt precision/recall table. That run will need the annotated set from Junction to compute recall — without it we can only provide internal concordance metrics.

On concordance thresholds: the 85% number was a pragmatic starting point we use for non-clinical flows. For triage it's reasonable to push to 92%+ for precision; let's surface both recall and precision in the matrix and call out an intermediate remediation threshold (88–92).

I'll own the smoke-run readiness checklist and aim to have the artifacts and the run results in Drive by Wed 24 Mar 17:00 PST. Priyom — please prepare a contracting lane note on the DPA template and any standard changes we request.

Marissa
Sr. Solution Architect | Redwood Inference

Elena / Sam —

Thanks for the fast feedback and for flagging security/legal timelines. Summary of agreed updates and owners below (I've updated the MAP in Drive with these changes):

- Security artifacts (Marissa) — deliver SOC2 summary + network diagram by Wed 24 Mar 17:00 PST. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Jx-example-MAP-folder
- Annotated sample set (Junction) — Elena / Sam to share an S3 path or limited CSV export by Wed 24th COB so we can compute recall.
- Acceptance thresholds (Marissa) — revise matrix to include precision & recall targets: target precision >= 92% (green), remediation 88–92% (yellow), <88% (red).
- Contracting & DPA (Priyom) — draft DPA with 90-day retention options for test data; Priyom to circulate a redline by Fri 26 Mar.
- Pilot smoke-run (Marissa) — tentatively scheduled 28 Mar pending security evidence; if artifacts are delayed we'll slide to 1 Apr.

Next step: Elena, can you confirm by EOD tomorrow whether Junction can share the annotated set? If yes, we'll keep 28 Mar as the smoke-run date and execute acceptance tests immediately after.

If useful I can set a 30-min sync with security + procurement this week to unblock the artifacts faster.

Best —
